verified.name: Engine Ventures
verified.thesis: Engine Ventures invests in early-stage Tough Tech companies solving the world's most important challenges through breakthrough science and engineering. The firm focuses on hardware-based technologies across deep tech fields including biotech, robotics, green energy, agriculture, manufacturing, material science, and quantum computing.
verified.notes: Engine Ventures is a separate investment firm that spun out from The Engine (a nonprofit incubator/accelerator) in 2023. Sources do not provide current AUM or flagship fund name for Engine Ventures specifically. Key partners for Engine Ventures are not identified in provided sources. Wikipedia lists Emily Knight as CEO & President of The Engine (the parent nonprofit), not Engine Ventures directly.

changesProposed.name: Y Combinator

verified.name: Y Combinator
verified.thesis: Y Combinator invests $500,000 per company ($125,000 for 7% equity on a post-money SAFE and $375,000 on an uncapped SAFE with an MFN clause) in startups selected four times per year. Founders move to San Francisco for three months of intensive mentorship, office hours, and community support, culminating in Demo Day where they present to investors.
verified.notes: Garry Tan became President and CEO in January 2023 (source 2). Jared Friedman succeeded Michael Seibel as Managing Partner in March 2024 (source 2). Headquarters moved from Mountain View to San Francisco in spring 2023 (source 2). Source [3] is unrelated to Y Combinator (article about Definium Therapeutics) and was not used.
